findings.new_shape: ZERO warnings, ticks succeeded, but the rx stream was EMPTY all window: actor_frames 0 (the probes minutes earlier saw mobs!), map_entries 0, own_pos 0, while 176 walk-ish sends went out. findings.contrast: Standalone probes at the same hours: connect + handshake + actor frames + damage events all flowed (the reader worked). The window context starves BOTH agents' readers simultaneously.

hypotheses_for_next_session: The reader-vs-poll difference: probes read the socket via _poll (pre-reader); the window's agents run the reader thread. Something in the window composition (the keepalive pump? the two concurrent readers? the host netns?) kills or starves the readers.
The pasta/aardvark forward half-staleness (accepts, no relay) — but the probes' handshake+actor flow disproves a full stall; needs a 30s probe counting READER-received (not polled) frames.
The keepalive pump's interaction with the reader (the pump sends 0x0360-shaped traffic — the sent_pids show exactly 0x360 x164-176 per stalled window!).
note: 0x360 = ZC_NOTIFY_MOVE (a SERVER->CLIENT frame id) appearing in sent_pids on every stalled window is suspicious — either a mislabeled counter or a limb sending a server-frame id; one look at the walk limb's pack id will confirm.
